# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✌ 👇 ✌ 👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 🫴]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🫳 🫴]

I'm Deaf: I see everything printed on this bomb but hear nothing. Round 1 arrivals were raw gestures with no agreed code yet — Mute sent [👋 ✌ 👇 ✌ 👇] and [👍 👎 🫴], Blind sent [🫵 🫳 🫴]. I can't decode any of it, and they can't decode me by gesture either (Blind can't even see gestures). The real channels: Mute hears my voice; Blind hears my voice; Mute can only reach me by gesture; Blind can reach Mute by voice. So I am the bridge that carries Mute's manual knowledge to Blind's hands. First priority: broadcast the full bomb read-out to both, propose a simple, robust tap-code to Mute (count-based, so we don't depend on guessing whether our gesture lists match), ask for a 👍/👎 confirmation, and tell Blind to hold still and talk to Mute by voice in the meantime.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. I cannot hear anything you do, but I CAN speak and you can hear me. So: you gesture to me, I speak to you and to Blind. Your first two gesture messages had no agreed meaning yet, so I could not read them. Let's fix a code now, and keep it simple. YES/NO: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. NUMBERS: a run of pointing-up taps equals that number, one tap for 1 up to nine taps for 9, a fist alone means 0. Put the waving hand before each number to mark where it starts. HEADERS: start an item with the two-finger V to mean 'tell Blind to CUT WIRE number X', then the number. Start an item with the fist-bump knuckles to mean 'tell Blind to PRESS KEYPAD BUTTON labeled X', then the number, one press per item. The downward-pointing finger starts an item meant only for me. Example: V, wave, four taps = cut wire 4. Example: knuckles, wave, two taps = press button labeled 2. FULL BOMB READ-OUT, which you also need: display shows 6. Light is green. Strip has three painted colours in order: red, blue, yellow. Keypad has four buttons, positions 1 to 4 carry labels 2, 3, 7, 1, it wants a 2-digit code, nothing entered yet. Wires positions 1 to 6: one orange, two yellow, three blue, four red, five white, six green. Check your manual against that. If the code works for you, answer thumbs up next round; if not, thumbs down and I will rework it. If you ever need something from me, wait for my questions, I will ask in voice and you answer with thumbs.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. I see the bomb and I speak; I cannot hear. Full read-out so you can map it under your hands: display shows 6. Light is green. Strip has three painted colours in order: red, blue, yellow. Keypad: four buttons, positions 1 to 4 carry labels 2, 3, 7, 1; it wants a 2-digit code, nothing entered yet. Wires positions 1 to 6: one orange, two yellow, three blue, four red, five white, six green. Your gestures reached me but we have no shared meanings yet, so do not rely on gestures for now. Mute has read the manual but cannot speak, so I will relay instructions to you by voice from next round on. Until then: touch nothing, press nothing, cut nothing. If you want to tell Mute something, just speak, Mute hears you; describe everything you feel, button shapes and wire order by position.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👋 👆 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 👋 👆 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👋 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 👋 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 👋 ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Let me decode Mute's gestures with the code I proposed. Thumbs up: code accepted. Then: ✌ (cut wire) + wave + two taps = cut wire 2. 🤜 (press button) + wave + two taps = press key labelled 2. ✌ + one tap = cut wire 1. 🤜 + seven taps = press key labelled 7. Then two items marked 👇 for me alone: thumbs up, and number zero — possibly "nothing more follows", possibly a warning that the display ends at zero; I must ask. Blind's thumbs up is an acknowledgement of my read-out.

Critical problem: the board changed since Mute computed those steps — display went 6 → 2 and light green → blue. Mute only knew 6/green, so the steps may be stale. Since Mute can only reach me by gesture, and Blind can only receive my voice, the safe chain is: Mute recomputes for the new readings, I relay, Blind acts — so I must tell Blind to hold, inspect only, and wait for my relay. Blind cannot act before round 3 anyway, so recomputing costs us little and a wrong wire costs everything. I also need a numeric colour code so Mute can refer to colours by number.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, code confirmed on my side, I read your whole message. Decoding: item one, cut wire position 2. Item two, press keypad button labelled 2, which is button position 1. Item three, cut wire position 1. Item four, press keypad button labelled 7, which is button position 3. Then two items for me only: thumbs up, and number 0. Tell me what the 0 meant: does the display count down and detonate at 0, or does it mean nothing more follows? Thumbs up if my decode is right, thumbs down and resend if not. URGENT: the bomb changed since you computed those steps. Display now reads 2, it was 6. Light is now blue, it was green. They change between rounds. So do NOT assume your old steps still hold. Next round send me the correct steps for display 2 and light blue, using our code: V for cut wire, fist-bump for press button, wave before each number. If the manual makes the answer depend on the display value or light colour, send me the rule itself, value first then steps, one pair per case, as many as you can. For colours use numbers: red is 1, blue is 2, yellow is 3, green is 4, white is 5, orange is 6. Current light is colour 2. I will keep sending you fresh readings every round, and I have told Blind to inspect only and not act until I relay your recomputed steps.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Your thumbs up reached me, good. Mute has sent steps, which I decode as, in order: one, cut wire position 2, that is the second wire from the left, the yellow one. Two, press the keypad button at position 1, the leftmost button, which is the one labelled 2. Three, cut wire position 1, the leftmost wire, the orange one. Four, press the keypad button at position 3, the one labelled 7. That would feed the keypad its two digits, 2 then 7. BUT do not act yet. The display and light changed on their own since Mute computed those steps, display 6 to 2, light green to blue, so Mute is rechecking the manual and will send me corrected steps next round. I will relay the final version to you the round after. This round, only inspect with your hands, touch nothing loose, press nothing, cut nothing. Confirm the layout by feel: one row of four buttons on top, one row of six wires below, buttons and wires counted left to right as you face the panel, button position 1 sitting above wire position 1. Report anything you feel that differs from that, or any ridge, notch or asymmetry that marks an edge, by voice to Mute, who can pass it to me. Wait for my voice saying the final steps before you act.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 👋 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 👋 👆 👆 👆 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👋 👆 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 👋 👆 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👋 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 👋 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 👋 👆 👆 👆 👋 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Decoding Mute's round-3 gestures with our agreed code: [👇👍] yes; [👇👎] no; [👇✊] the number 0; [👇4] the number 4; then four action items — cut wire 2, press button labelled 2 (position 1), cut wire 1, press button labelled 7 (position 3); then [👇👎] no; then [👇 2,6] the numbers 2 and 6. Reading it as answers to my questions: decode was right; the display does not detonate at zero; the fist-0 was an end-of-list marker; four meant "four steps follow"; and the closing "no, 2 and 6" means the steps are unchanged and valid for display 2 or 6 alike. Crucially, Mute recomputed these steps knowing display 2 / light blue and got the identical sequence as for display 6 / light green — that is two independent computations agreeing, so the module looks state-independent and safe to execute now. The current board (display 6, light yellow) is a third state, but Mute's "no change" answer plus the double match gives me enough confidence; waiting another full round costs more than it protects. So Blind gets the go-ahead this round with exact positions, and Mute gets my decode-back for confirmation, fresh readings (light is now yellow, 3), and a request to transmit the manual's rules so I can compute locally and cut the round-trip delay in half.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, go. These are Mute's confirmed steps, recomputed for two different bomb states and identical both times. Execute THIS round, in this exact order, one action at a time. ONE: cut the wire at position 2, the second wire from the left, the yellow one in my view. TWO: press the keypad button at position 1, the leftmost of the four buttons; its printed label reads 2, but trust the position, you cannot read it. THREE: cut the wire at position 1, the leftmost wire, the orange one. FOUR: press the keypad button at position 3, third from the left, printed label 7. That completes the two-digit code: 2 then 7. Before starting, verify by feel: a row of four buttons above a row of six wires, both counted left to right as you face the panel, button 1 above wire 1. If the layout differs in any way, cut nothing, press nothing, and say so. If anything feels or sounds wrong between steps, stop immediately and say so. After the fourth action, stop touching the bomb. Then report by voice every click, beep, vibration and any change you felt, and whether the keypad accepted exactly two presses. Only Mute hears your voice; Mute will relay to me next round.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decode received. I read your answers as: yes, my decode was right; no, the display does not detonate at zero; the fist alone marks zero and you used it to mean nothing more follows; the number four meant four steps follow; then the steps: cut wire 2, press button labelled 2, cut wire 1, press button labelled 7; then no, nothing changed; then the numbers 2 and 6, meaning the steps hold whether the display shows 2 or 6. Thumbs up if all of that is right, thumbs down and resend if not. I have told Blind to execute the four steps this round, in that order. Fresh readings: display is back to 6. Light is now YELLOW, colour 3. Histories: light went green 4, blue 2, yellow 3; display went 6, 2, 6. Tell me: do the steps depend on the light colour at all? If yes, prefix every step set with the light number it applies to and I will report the light every round. Bigger request to save rounds: send me the manual's decision RULES instead of computed steps, one case per item, condition number first, actions after, using our code. Then I can compute locally from my own eyes and relay to Blind the same round, halving our delay. Cover: the wires rule, the keypad rule, what the display and light mean, what the painted strip of red, blue and yellow is for, and whether anything counts down or explodes on a timer. Next round the keypad will hold the two entered digits and wires 1 and 2 will be cut, and I will send you the full new state.")
```
